context.what_changed_since_iteration_1: Letflow.ServiceCatalog (lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex) gains one new, additive, read-only function, list_all/1 -- same list_params() input and {:ok, %{items:, next_cursor:}} | {:error, ...} output shape as the existing list_for_tenant/2, but with no tenant_id argument and the where([e], e.scope == :global or e.owner_tenant_id == ^tenant_id) clause omitted entirely (not replaced by a tautology). It reuses filter_by_list_cursor/2 verbatim and now-parameterized split_list_page/3 / build_list_next_cursor/2 (which previously hardcoded list_for_tenant/2's own 'SC:' cursor prefix -- refactored to take the prefix as an explicit argument specifically so list_all/1 could reuse the same page-splitting logic while still minting its own 'SCA:'-prefixed cursors; this refactor was necessary to satisfy INV-9 correctly and was not itself part of the approved design text, so it is called out here explicitly). list_all/1 has its own @list_all_cursor_prefix "SCA:" module attribute, distinct from list_for_tenant/2's "SC:" -- Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4's check_prefix/2 rejects a cursor minted by one if replayed against the other ({:error, :wrong_endpoint}). list_for_tenant/2 itself is byte-for-byte unchanged in name, arity, and where-clause; only its two now-private helper functions changed signature (gained a `prefix` parameter) to be shared safely.
context.admin_services_ex_change: lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex's GET / handler (handle_list/1) now calls Letflow.ServiceCatalog.list_all(params) instead of building its own Ecto.Query against Entry. All router-local query-building code (the former private list_all/1, filter_by_list_cursor/2, decode_list_cursor/1, decode_seek/1, split_list_page/2, build_list_next_cursor/1) was deleted from this file, along with the `import Ecto.Query` and `alias Letflow.Repo` it required. `alias Letflow.ServiceCatalog.Entry` is retained -- still needed for this router's own service_record_json/1 @spec and pattern match, which is unrelated to the query-building removed above. task.description: Re-review the two changed files (lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex's new list_all/1, and lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex's rewritten GET / handler) against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md (INV-4, INV-7, INV-8 apply at this stage). The security-critical question specific to this rework: list_all/1 performs ZERO tenant or scope filtering by design -- it is a genuinely global, unfiltered read across the entire service_catalog table, intended for exactly one caller (the GET /admin/services handler). Confirm this is safe by verifying, independently and by direct code reading (not by trusting this handoff's claim): (1) Letflow.Api.Authorization.endpoint_policy_key/2 genuinely maps GET "/admin/services" to :AdminServicesRead (not :ServicesRead or any other key) with no path-matching ambiguity against GET "/services"; (2) Letflow.Api.Authorization.required_permission/1 genuinely maps :AdminServicesRead to :UsersGroupsRolesManage; (3) Letflow.Api.Authorization.role_allows?/2's matrix genuinely grants :UsersGroupsRolesManage to :PLATFORM_ADMIN alone, not to :PROCESS_DESIGNER/:PROCESS_OPERATOR/:TASK_WORKER/:AGENT_RUNNER; (4) Letflow.Plugs.Authorize (or whichever plug consumes endpoint_policy_key/2's result) genuinely runs BEFORE handle_list/1 is ever invoked, i.e. this is a real, load-bearing plug-pipeline gate and not something a router-level bug could bypass; (5) confirm list_all/1's own @doc in lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex states plainly that it performs no filtering and that authorization is entirely the caller's responsibility -- so a future caller of this function from a different, less-trusted route cannot mistake it for a safe default. Also verify the two 409 problem-details bodies (service_referenced_by_active_definitions/1, service_scope_narrowing_conflict/1) still do not leak data beyond what Letflow.ServiceCatalog.delete/1 and update_scope/2 themselves already decided to disclose (unchanged from iteration 1, but re-confirm since this is the review of record for this iteration).
acceptance_criteria: Independently confirmed (by reading lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex directly, not by trusting this handoff) that GET /admin/services resolves to :AdminServicesRead -> :UsersGroupsRolesManage -> PLATFORM_ADMIN-only, with no role other than :PLATFORM_ADMIN able to reach handle_list/1

Independently confirmed that the plug pipeline (Letflow.Plugs.Authorize or equivalent) genuinely enforces this gate ahead of the handler, not merely that the router module declares the right policy key

list_all/1's complete absence of tenant/scope filtering is confirmed to be exactly what its @doc states, with no hidden partial filter and no dead code path that could accidentally apply narrower or wider visibility than documented
Both new Error constructors' extensions maps re-confirmed to leak no data beyond what delete/1 and update_scope/2 already return
grep -rn "Repo\." lib/letflow/routers/ independently re-run and confirmed to have zero live-code (non-comment, non-moduledoc) matches

Explicit AGREE or DISAGREE recorded on whether the router-level authorization gate is a sufficient, correctly-scoped substitute for list_all/1's own complete lack of tenant isolation -- this is the central security question this rework introduces
